focus-anesthetic.title: Common anesthetic medications
focus-anesthetic.text: Recognize the separate roles of hypnosis, amnesia, analgesia, neuromuscular paralysis and regional anesthesia. A specific antagonist exists for opioids (naloxone) and benzodiazepines (flumazenil); sugammadex targets rocuronium/vecuronium, and neostigmine can antagonize adequately recovered nondepolarizing blockade. Most anesthetics have no drug-specific reversal. Dantrolene treats MH; lipid emulsion treats severe LAST, not routine anesthesia reversal.

focus-precautions.title: Transmission-based precautions
focus-precautions.text: Routine practices apply to everyone. ORNAC §2.2 gives examples of airborne, droplet, and contact infections; some require combined precautions. This set differentiates ordinary disease isolation from additional respiratory protection during specific aerosol-generating tasks. Local IPAC requirements and patient factors prevail.

focus-periop-meds.title: Perioperative medication risk
focus-periop-meds.text: Reconcile prescription drugs, OTC medications, and supplements. Know the medication class and its primary perioperative risks: bleeding/thrombosis, fasting hypoglycemia, euglycemic ketoacidosis, aspiration, hemodynamic effects, adrenal suppression, drug interactions, and withdrawal. These are recognition questions, not universal stop/continue orders.
